problem_class.label: other
problem_class.details: Unconstrained monotone root finding: find an approximate zero of a continuous operator F:E→E satisfying ⟨F(x)−F(y),x−y⟩≥0. E is an arbitrary real inner-product space; completeness and finite dimensionality are not required. No objective or saddle function is specified.

oracle.label: other
oracle.details: Exact operator-value oracle: every query x returns F(x), for every call index and seed. There is no oracle error or sample dependence. Each evaluation counts as one oracle call under a fixed budget.

setup_category.reason: Monotone root finding is established, but this setup replaces global Lipschitz continuity with an operator-magnitude-dependent segment condition and requires a constructor independent of the hidden radius, initial residual bound, and tolerance.

descriptionHtml:
Generalized Lipschitz Monotone Root Finding

We seek a zero of a continuous monotone operator F:E→E on a real inner product space E with induced norm ∥⋅∥. For constants L0>0 and L1≥0, the Lipschitz bound along each segment is L0+L1M whenever M bounds the norm of F on that segment. A given point x0∈E satisfies ∥F(x0)∥≤G and lies within distance R of a zero, where G,R≥0. The oracle returns F(x) at x. For ε>0, the goal is an output x¯∈E with ∥F(x¯)∥≤ε almost surely under P, the law of the algorithm’s randomness.

The root-finding problem is to find x∈E such that F(x)=0. Write ⟨⋅,⋅⟩ for the inner product on E. The algorithm receives only E, L0, L1, and x0; the residual bound G, radius R, and tolerance ε may enter the oracle-call budget but are not algorithm inputs.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Continuity and monotonicity). The operator F is continuous, and for every x,y∈E, ⟨F(x)−F(y),x−y⟩≥0.

Assumption 2 (Generalized Lipschitz condition). For every x,y∈E and M∈R satisfying ∥F(x+θ(y−x))∥≤Mfor every θ∈[0,1], the operator satisfies ∥F(x)−F(y)∥≤(L0+L1M)∥x−y∥.

Assumption 3 (Initial residual and distance). There exists x⋆∈E such that F(x⋆)=0,∥x0−x⋆∥≤R,∥F(x0)∥≤G.

Queries may be made at any point of E. After the allotted oracle calls, the output must satisfy the residual criterion ∥F(x¯)∥≤εP-a.s.

comparisonHtml:
A continuous monotone map F:E→E on a real inner-product space satisfies ∥F(x)−F(y)∥≤(L0+L1max0≤t≤1∥F(x+t(y−x))∥)∥x−y∥. Here L0>0, L1,G,R≥0, ε>0, ∥F(x0)∥≤G, and some root x⋆ satisfies ∥x0−x⋆∥≤R. The oracle returns exact F(x); the target is ∥F(x)∥≤ε deterministically. The setup imposes no algorithm restriction.

Exact monotone root finding under GeneralizedLipschitzMonotone.
Result Oracle complexity Novelty Limitations
(1) AnchoredGeneralizedMonotone (Ours) (⋆⋆⋆) (review) O(1+L0Rε+(1+L1R)⋅log(1+(L0+L1G)Rε)). Also O(1+L0R/ε+L12R2) using the intrinsic initial-residual bound.
(2) EG (Choudhury and Loizou 2025, Thm. 3.6) O(1+L02R2/ε2+L12R2). E=Rd. (1): L0R/ε instead of (L0R/ε)2; speedup Θ(L0R/ε) if ε≤min{L0R,L0/(L12R)}. Scope: arbitrary real inner-product spaces. For L0=L1=1, R=10, ε=10−3: O(104) versus O(108).
(3) PolyakEG (Yoon et al. 2026, Thm. 3.4, Eq. (19)) O(1+L02R2/ε2+L12R2). Known L0,L1; E=Rd. (1): same leading-term gain as against (2). If L1>0 and L0/(L12R)≤ε≤L0/L1, speedup Ω((L0/(L1ε))2). For ε≥L0/L1, moderate G gives L1Rlog⁡(2+L1R+L0R/ε) instead of L12R2; otherwise no strict gain is assured.
(4) PolyakEG-LS (Yoon et al. 2026, Thm. 3.4, Prop. 3.5(a)) Derived bound: O(1+B+(λ¯0)2R2ε2+(λ¯1)2R2), including all trials. E=Rd; fixed A∈(0,1), β>2, positive initial estimates λ0,λ1. (1): ε−1 instead of ε−2 for fixed remaining parameters; no backtracking calls. Last iterate instead of minimum residual among observed iterates. (1) needs L0,L1 in its updates; (4) does not.
(5) FEG / EAG (Lee and Kim 2021, Thm. 4.1, ρ=0)(Yoon and Ryu 2021, Thms. 1–2, Sec. 2.3) O(1+L0R/ε). Special case: L1=0, E=Rd. (1) matches the known rate on this overlap; scope extends to generalized Lipschitz continuity with L1>0. (1) has a roughly fivefold larger leading cost constant than FEG when L1=0.

Abbr: Costs count individual F-evaluations. R: initial root-distance bound; G: initial residual bound; ε: residual tolerance. The intrinsic bound is ∥F(x0)∥≤L0ReL1R, so G may be replaced by min{G,L0ReL1R}. Moderate G means log⁡(1+L1G/L0)=O(log⁡(2+L1R)). For (4), A is the fixed acceptance tolerance, β the backtracking factor, λi the initial estimates, B=2max{0,⌈log⁡(L0/λ0)/log⁡(β−1)⌉,⌈log⁡(L1/λ1)/log⁡(β−1)⌉}, and λ¯i=βB/2λi; omit the L1 logarithm when L1=0. In (2), interpret L0/(L12R)=+∞ if L1R=0.

import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.Basic
import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Measure.ProbabilityMeasure
import LongTails.Template

open scoped RealInnerProductSpace

namespace LongTails.Setups.GeneralizedLipschitzMonotone

open OracleTemplate

structure Public where
  E : Type u
  [normedE : NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [linearE : InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
  L0 : ℝ
  L1 : ℝ
  x0 : E

attribute [instance] Public.normedE Public.linearE

structure Params extends Public where
  G : ℝ
  R : ℝ
  ε : ℝ

abbrev spec : Setup where
  Params := Params
  Public := Public
  Instance p := p.E → p.E
  Query p := p.E
  Reply p := p.E
  Output p := p.E
  publicInput := Params.toPublic
  valid q := 0 < q.L0 ∧ 0 ≤ q.L1 ∧ 0 ≤ q.G ∧ 0 ≤ q.R ∧ 0 < q.ε
  admissible q F oracle :=
    (∀ k seed x, oracle.answer k (0, x) seed = F x) ∧
    Continuous F ∧
    (∀ x y, 0 ≤ ⟪F x - F y, x - y⟫) ∧
    (∀ x y M, (∀ θ ∈ Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, ‖F (x + θ • (y - x))‖ ≤ M) →
      ‖F x - F y‖ ≤ (q.L0 + q.L1 * M) * ‖x - y‖) ∧
    ‖F q.x0‖ ≤ q.G ∧
    (∃ xstar, F xstar = 0 ∧ ‖q.x0 - xstar‖ ≤ q.R)
  successful q F output P :=
    ∀ᵐ ω ∂(P : MeasureTheory.Measure _), ‖F (output ω)‖ ≤ q.ε

end LongTails.Setups.GeneralizedLipschitzMonotone
